scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported Andyamathanha destination covers 1600–1815 in the Flinders Ranges region. The standard name Adnyamathanha is used, retaining the imported spelling as an alias. The dates remain map coverage, with no artificial fall or replacement people.

Warratyi is on Adnyamathanha country. Its archaeological sequence is not proof of an unchanged ethnic name, fixed polity or language over 49,000 years. The card does not adopt the press-release claim that it is the oldest site on the entire continent, or infer continuous occupation from every layer.

The original Hamm et al. article was read in the author/project copy at https://webcreator.com.au/warratyi/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Hamm-et-al-Nature-Warratyi.pdf . The source budget combines this copy with the Nature article. Dates are approximate archaeological estimates, not dates of invention.

The bone point’s possible skin-working function is explicitly comparative. Residue evidence supports hafting, not a specific weapon function. Exact hafting-age ranges differ between abstract and main discussion, so no falsely precise single date is assigned.
The card does not assert that Diprotodon bones prove deliberate hunting, name an eggshell taxon amid the paper’s uncertainty, or invent a painted motif from ochre residues.

Museums Victoria’s item has an unrecorded maker. It is not attributed to a named Coulthard family carver without evidence. The approximately 1930 production and approximately 1995 collection dates are kept distinct. The physical description is from the catalogue; collection photographs were not independently inspected.

The museum’s statement about continuous occupation and the university press release’s mistranslation of coolamons as walking sticks are not adopted. The separate family-carving account names objects directly supported by the SA Museum exhibition text.

Nepabunna’s own account supports the 1930s phase and the effects of pastoral settlement. A specific 1931 mission founding requires a separate source and is not inferred from that broad community account.

Iga Warta’s brochure is used for its own teaching and food practices, not current prices or booking advice. Its unsupported precise age for a painting site is not repeated, and modern dishes are not presented as Pleistocene food.
The 2005 National Reserve System case study supports historical management and training. Its contemporary status at publication is not portrayed as an independently measured 2026 ecological result.

The 2009 register describes three related determinations and their differing exclusive/non-exclusive scope. The card focuses on the specified park rights, not a simplified claim of blanket ownership. The register extract date is not the determination date; later litigation is not inferred.
The 2013 ATLA report distinguishes an accomplished resort purchase from employment targets. No claim is made that all targets were met or that the report’s institutional roster remains current.
The dictionary contents and authorship are described from the Mobile Language Team’s participant account; the full book was not inspected. Its launch is 2020, not the upload or crawl date.
Independent historical review, identity and border verification, and depth certification remain pending.
